blocks.content:
ScanSSD: Scanning Single Shot Detector for
Mathematical Formulas in PDF Document Images
Parag Mali, Puneeth Kukkadapu, Mahshad Mahdavi, and, Richard Zanibbi
Department of Computer Science, Rochester Institute of Technology
Rochester, NY 14623, USA
Email: {psm2208, pxk8301, mxm7832, rxzvcs}@rit.edu
Abstract—We introduce the Scanning Single Shot Detector
(ScanSSD) for locating math formulas offset from text and
embedded in textlines. ScanSSD uses only visual features for
detection: no formatting or typesetting information such as
layout, font, or character labels are employed. Given a 600 dpi

Fig. 2 output: page 745 with one green bounding box per detected formula (inline items such as k(t,s), [0,1] and displayed equations (2.1)-(2.8)) after pooling.

Fig. 3: default boxes for a 512x512 window. A grid of blue star box centres covers a page crop; six rectangles (red, green, yellow) of different sizes and aspect ratios surround the pink-highlighted formula u'' = 0.

Fig. 2 sliding-window sub-image: an unannotated crop of the scanned page showing the BVP text and equations u'' = 0, alpha u(0) - beta u'(0) = 0, gamma u(1) + delta u'(1) = 0 (window offsets differ between the stacked crops).

Fig. 2 input page: unannotated scan of a journal page headed 'POSITIVE SOLUTIONS OF ORDINARY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS 745', with numbered equations (2.1)-(2.8) defining k(t,s), the cone K and the operator A.

Fig. 2 stitched-heatmap page: page 745 thumbnail with greyed background and heatmap highlights (white, pink, yellow) over formula regions, after stitching window-level detections.
Fig. 2 stitched-patches page: page 745 thumbnail covered with dense overlapping purple bounding boxes from window-level detections, before pooling.

Fig. 4: histogram of formula aspect ratios. Y-axis 'Count' with ticks 0, 2500, 5000, 7500, 10000; x-axis 'Aspect ratio' 1 to 38. Bars peak at ratio 2 (about 9000) and 1 (about 8400), then fall steadily (about 5000 at 3, 4500 at 4, 2900 at 5) to near zero beyond about 20.

Fig. 5(a) base image: scanned excerpt with equations (2.1) u'' = 0 and (2.2) the two boundary conditions. In the rendered figure a blue detection box sits on the first boundary condition; that box is not in this extracted image.
Fig. 5(b) base image: the same scanned excerpt (equations (2.1), (2.2)) used for the 'After cropping' panel; the cropped blue box shown in the paper is not part of this extracted image.

Fig. 6 panel 4: detection results on page 744 of Erbe and Wang ('2. Existence results', Theorem 1, Corollary 1, Theorem 2 of Krasnoselskii), with blue bounding boxes around inline and displayed formulas.

Fig. 6 panel 1: detection results on a page about quadratic relations among codimension-zero classes (equations (3.3)-(3.5)), each formula enclosed in a blue bounding box, wide multi-line sums boxed line by line.

Fig. 6 panel 2: detection results on a page containing (5.23), 'Nonsingular rational curves', 'Quantum multiplication in H*(P^n)', (5.24) and a matrix D-module equation, with blue bounding boxes around formulas.

Fig. 6 panel 3: detection results on page 745 of the ODE article (equations (2.1)-(2.8)), with blue bounding boxes; per the caption, split formulas are highlighted in pink in this panel, which is not clearly visible in the extracted image.

Fig. 7: document-level f-scores for 10 test documents (Lorentz48, Jones83, Lusztig89, Kontsevich94, Erbe94, Gidas79, Kazhdan79, Li75, Emden76, Katz99). Blue bars IOU >= 0.5 range 0.6816 (Emden76) to 0.8787 (Erbe94); red bars IOU >= 0.75 range 0.5898 (Emden76) to 0.8518 (Erbe94); y-axis 0.5 to 0.9.
